findings_fixed: The PHP sitemap (cloudhost247-sitemap.php) filtered by publication state only, so it advertised submitticket.php while robots.txt disallowed it. Sitemaps and robots.txt now read one registry policy, and the build fails if the policy excludes a registered public page, a published tool category or a sitemap endpoint.

Sitemap endpoints (cloudhost247-sitemap.php, tools-sitemap.php, builder-sitemap.php, robots.php) were themselves listed as disallowed while robots.txt advertised them as Sitemap: — a disallowed sitemap cannot be fetched, which silently voids the directive. They are now excluded from the policy and send X-Robots-Tag: noindex instead.

robots.php kept its own hand-written private-path list, and the static robots.txt a third one. Both now read CloudHost247\Theme\CrawlPolicy, whose compiled fallback must equal the registry (asserted).

The static robots.txt disallowed /cloudhost247-page.php, the canonical URL of every CMS-authored page the sitemap lists. The route stays crawlable; only the internal sample and element pages are excluded.

The tool surface published two category taxonomies: the menus advertised the nine discovery categories, while the native PHP catalogue (config/tools.php), the tools hub navigation and tools-sitemap.php used the engine grouping (dns, ip, designer, gaming…). Eight of the nine published category URLs resolved only through the theme fallback, and the sitemap advertised nine category URLs no navigation surface linked to. The native catalogue now resolves the discovery taxonomy, the hub and breadcrumbs publish it, the sitemap lists it, and the generator asserts parity between the registry, src/tools/catalog.ts and tools.json.

Node /robots.txt published only the single-page-app half of the crawl policy, so the file answering /robots.txt contradicted the rules the PHP surface obeys. It now publishes both halves, with rules normalised to root-relative paths (a registry entry written as admin/ previously produced an invalid Disallow: admin/ line).

Nine of the ten tool-category links published by the header and footer pointed at slugs no engine could resolve (the registry carried the legacy PHP engine's slugs, while the theme runtime and the React Tools Center both serve the discovery categories). The registry now publishes dns-domains, ip-network, security, ssl, email, website, developer, calculators and utilities, and a new Node test pins every published category to a non-empty catalogue category.

The Tools mega menu published zero links on the PHP surface (empty groups) and the PHP integration suite failed on it; the menu now publishes the nine server-rendered category floors, and the suite validates all of them.
The MRZ tool - a registered, public, browser-only tool - was missing from the PHP footer Tools column. It is now published with the agreed label.

The generator and scripts/verify-website.py validated PHP tool destinations against the legacy tools-public.json only; both now accept the authoritative theme projection tools.json (the file the PHP runtime reads) as well.
The PHP website suite asserted 'all seven mega menu categories'; it now pins the nine published families by id, matching the SPA.

docs/NODE_PLATFORM_STATUS.md was published as a public documentation page at /docs/node-platform-status. It is the internal phase-acceptance ledger (branch names, pull-request numbers, commit hashes, migrations that are prepared but not executed), so it was removed from the published set and stays in the repository for engineers.

De-publishing a document only removed it from the index: the markdown file stayed in frontend/public/docs and was still served and crawled. The generator now prunes de-published files from the build output and reports each removal.
